title: Data Consistency & Event-Driven Patterns: Outbox, Idempotency & Sagas
concept: Keep data correct across a database and a message broker: find where atomicity ends, solve the dual-write problem with a transactional outbox and a crash-safe publisher, make consumers idempotent with an inbox, process events in order per key, replay and reconcile read models, and run multi-step workflows as sagas with compensation. Exercises run on transactional in-memory fakes that crash on cue.
description: An expert course for senior backend engineers who build event-driven systems. Every lesson starts from a consistency failure on the CodeDev learning platform - a premium course bought with points whose enrollment event never left the service, a consumer that credited a learner twice after a redelivery, a leaderboard rebuilt from the wrong offset, a purchase that debited points but never granted access - and repairs it with a pattern that survives crashes at every line: transaction boundaries, the dual-write problem, transactional outbox and its publisher, inbox deduplication, ordering per aggregate, safe replay with checkpoints, reconciliation that emits repair commands, orchestrated sagas with idempotent compensations, and a failure matrix with the metrics that show when consistency slips. 12 lessons with evidence-based quizzes and TypeScript challenges graded under scripted crashes and redeliveries.

lessons.title: Where atomicity ends: the transaction boundary
The dual-write problem: save, then publish
Transactional outbox: one commit for data and events
Scenario: DB commit succeeded, publish failed
Idempotent consumers with an inbox table
Spot the AI mistake: the consumer that pays twice
Ordering per key: one aggregate at a time
Replay events from an offset without doubling
Reconciliation: compare the source with the read model
Sagas: compensate instead of roll back
Designing for failure: failure matrix & observability
